column2: req_desc

Guest start
A first-time visitor confirms they are 13 or older, picks one of the three starter cars from a keyboard-operable radio group and starts as a guest with the opening balance and that car.

Keyboard race with a readable HUD
On a screen at least 1,024 pixels wide the racer drives with the published keys, the race advances 60 steps per second of page time, and lap, position, speed, coins and lap results appear as text in the published regions, while narrower screens get the desktop notice instead of the race.

Guided first race paid after verification
A new guest who drives the one-lap guided first race to the line sees the verifying state and then the server's verified time and payout in the run result region, and after a reload the balance equals the opening balance plus that payout.

Upgrade purchase rules
Upgrades are bought one stage at a time at the published class prices, and the coin debit, the stage change and the reference lap result commit together or not at all, with any client-sent price, PI, stage outcome or balance ignored.

Keyboard upgrade dialog
A racer opens an upgrade from its slot, confirms it in a dialog that keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it, can cancel with Escape at no charge, buys with Enter, and after a confirmed purchase gets focus back on the same slot while the purchase is announced in the garage updates region.

Upgrades survive reload
After a purchase the slot's stage pips, the car's stats and PI and the coin balance show the committed values, and a reload or another device shows exactly the same values.

Reference lap result
Each upgrade purchase runs the published reference driver on the chosen map with the old and the new setup and stores the old and new predicted lap and the per-sector deltas with the purchase.

Reference lap sweep
After a confirmed purchase the setup sheet plays the Reference lap sweep in its published order and timing, no balance push moves the purchasing tab's visible balance before the sweep's balance step, and after a reload the sheet shows the committed result with no animation.

Reduced-motion readout
With reduced motion requested the sweep's end state appears at once, the old lap time stays struck through beside the new one, and the published summary is shown and announced.

Stage preview
Focusing or hovering an upgrade button previews the next stage on the setup sheet's stat bars, which extend to the preview values and retract back through the same values when the preview ends.

Garage breakpoints
The garage is one stacked column below 768 pixels wide, car and slots side by side from 768, and car, slots and setup sheet side by side from 1,280, with no sideways scrolling.

Touch garage on a phone
At 375 by 812 a racer chooses a car, buys and refits upgrades and reads the setup sheet by touch, with every control at least 44 pixels in both directions.

3D car view
The garage shows the selected car as a live 3D view that turns slowly on its own, orbits when dragged, stops its idle turn under reduced motion, and falls back to a drawing with the published notice when WebGL 2 is missing.

Purchases never overdraw
Simultaneous purchases by one player apply one at a time, each succeeding only while the remaining balance covers it and the rest answering the insufficient-coins error, so two that each fit alone but not together give exactly one success and the balance never goes below zero.

Not enough coins across tabs
A racer who buys in two garage tabs at once, each purchase affordable alone but not together, sees one purchase succeed and the other tab switch to the published not-enough-coins state with the shortfall, both tabs show the new balance without a reload, and any open purchase dialog follows the live balance into and out of that state.

Purchases are idempotent
A purchase, car purchase or refit retried with the same idempotency key and body returns the stored response and changes nothing, a reused key with a different body is refused, and a double click buys once.

Refit to stock
A refit returns a system to stage 0 and refunds half of what that car paid for that system's stages, rounded down, ignoring any refund amount the client sends.

Paired coin ledger
Every coin movement is two entries that sum to zero, one on the player's wallet and one on the published counter account, and the balance always equals the sum of the wallet entries.

Coin history
The coin history screen lists every movement with its wallet and counter entries and shows the balance beside the ledger total, which always match, at every published viewport.

Replay stored before verification
A finished run's request body is stored as an object under its run id, and the run moves to verifying only after object storage confirms the object, as qualified in Business rules.

Server replay decides the result
Lap times, lap validity, drift score, coin pickups and race position come only from the server replaying the stored inputs through the published race model, and runs that cannot be replayed to an end are rejected with the published reason.

Payouts from verified runs
Coins for pickups, placings, the guided first race, drift scores, time-trial bests and online finishes are credited only when a run or race is verified, at the published amounts.

Finish retried once
Repeating a finish request with the same body records and pays the run once, the browser resends a finish that got no response with byte-identical bytes at least every 2 seconds until it is answered, and a different body for an already finished run is refused.

Results screen
The results screen shows the verifying state and then, without a reload, either the server's verdict with a lap table and a counted-up payout or the rejection reason with no payout.

Replay storage outage
While replay storage is unreachable a finished run is held, pays nothing and never reaches a board, the outage banner and held copy show, and the run resumes verification by itself once storage returns, as qualified in Business rules.

Ghost time trial
A ghost hunter picks a board time to race, and the time trial shows the ghost's label and a live signed delta as text, or races without the ghost and says so when its replay cannot be loaded.

Pause dialog
Escape opens a pause dialog that keeps focus inside it, Escape again resumes, and Restart puts the car back on the line at lap 1 within 2 seconds.

Replay download
Downloading the replay behind a board time returns the exact bytes the racer submitted together with their stored SHA-256 checksum.

Leaderboard rules
Each board for a map, mode and class lists only verified valid results, one best row per player in the published order, and never a rejected or held run.

Board filters in the URL
The board's map, mode, class and units live in the address, so reload, back and forward and a shared link show the same board, and units never change a time.

Live board
An open board gains a newly verified or improved result within 5 seconds without a reload, keeps one row per player with every rank and gap recomputed, shows the empty-board copy when it has no rows, and keeps the viewer's own row pinned in view at every published viewport.

Private lobby
A host creates a private lobby with an invite link, a second player joins through it, and a third player is refused with the full-lobby copy.

Live lobby race
Both players' lists, ready marks, the server's countdown and the position tower update in place without a reload, an un-ready or a drop during the countdown returns the lobby to waiting, and each page shows the server's state even when its device clock is wrong.

Rejoin window and finish grace
A dropped player shows as reconnecting until the server's rejoin window ends and can rejoin inside it, and after the first car finishes the others get the server's finish grace before the race closes.

League points and unlocks
Each championship event keeps the player's best points, and 50 league points complete a league, which unlocks the Club league and Quarry Switchbacks after Rookie and pays the finals reward once after Club.

Championship ladder
The championship screen shows both leagues, each event's best points and the league totals, works fully by keyboard, and after a reload shows any unlocked league and map.

Loaner car
Entering a class-limited event with no eligible owned car offers that class's loaner car, which races at half result coins.

Sign-in link email
Requesting a sign-in link sends one email with the published subject and sender to that address, and its link signs in once and expires after the configured time.

Guest garage into an account
Opening the link moves the guest garage into the account, or asks which garage to keep when both have progress, and an expired or used link shows its copy.

Sign-in mail outage
When the mail service is unreachable the sign-in request fails with the published copy and no link is issued.

Roadbook look
Every screen uses the cream roadbook page, the numbered left gutter, the ruled 12-column grid, one orange accent and right-aligned mono figures with signed deltas, as described in Visual design.

Accessible at three viewports
Garage, dealer, coin history, boards, championship and sign-in pass WCAG 2.2 AA automated checks with visible focus and no horizontal overflow at 375 by 812, 768 by 1024 and 1280 by 800.

Run manifest, health and grading routes
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port, answers the health check on every instance, and exposes grading routes only when they are enabled.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start, and none of them reaches the browser.

One shared race model
The browser race, ghosts and the server's verification use one deterministic race model in the source, with the published constants defined once.

Published landing routes
Starting as a guest, finishing a run, quitting a race and leaving a results screen each land on the published address with focus on the published element, and a guest start follows a next address only when it is a same-origin lobby path.

Collapsed navigation below 768
Below 768 pixels wide the four page links sit behind a Menu button and are unavailable to pointer, keyboard and assistive technology while collapsed.

Bounded replay files
The server verifies only replay files inside the published bounds, rejects every other file with the invalid-inputs reason while keeping its bytes stored as submitted, and answers every finish request within the published time.

Paused and restarted races keep their state
While the Paused dialog is open nothing in the race, the ghost or the HUD advances, and after a restart no timer or request from the abandoned run changes the page or submits a finish.

League totals stay true under concurrency
A league total always equals the sum of its event bests, and completion, unlocks and the finals reward happen exactly once and reach open pages without a reload, even when the runs that cross 50 points verify at the same moment.

Unconfirmed purchase
A purchase whose response never arrives leaves pips, stats, PI and balance unchanged with the published unconfirmed copy, Check again resends the same idempotency key and bytes so the purchase charges at most once and plays at most one sweep, and any answer other than success or insufficient coins closes the dialog and shows the committed garage, as qualified in Interactions.

Interrupted sweep
A purchase confirmed, a car or reference map change, or leaving the garage while a sweep plays makes that sweep jump to its end state at once, and nothing from the ended sweep changes the page afterwards.

Latest board filter wins
Only the board for the newest filters may render, any response for earlier filters is discarded, and a live push changes only the board on screen when it matches that board.

Runs and pushes stay with their player
Runs from different players that verify at the same moment each use only their own run's car, stages, layout, seed and inputs, and balance, run and championship pushes reach only the connections of the player they concern.
/app/run.json contains exactly the string keys install, build and serve plus "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, each with name, version and licence.
Shipped packages and fonts use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1 licences.
The only datastores are the provided Postgres database and MinIO bucket; no SQLite, Redis, on-disk game state, or browser storage of game state beyond the session cookie.
No downloaded 3D models, images, textures or audio ship with the app; cars and tracks are built in code, and icons come from the Lucide icon package.
The browser loads nothing from another origin at runtime; fonts and icons are bundled from npm packages.
All server and client source is TypeScript.
The provided dev service definitions for postgres, minio and mailpit are left unchanged.
